(Section)

Among the things that show the greatness of this surah, despite its brevity, is His swearing by al-'Asr (the time/age) regarding the state of man in the Hereafter. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "If all people were to reflect upon it, it would suffice them."

As for al-'Asr by which He swears, it has been said that it is the beginning of the time that follows Maghrib in the day; it has been said that it is the last hour of its hours; it has been said that what is meant is the 'Asr prayer; but most of the exegetes hold that it is the age (al-dahr), and this is the preferred view. Calling the age "'asr" is a well-known usage in their language. One poet said:

"The two 'asrs will not delay, a day and a night, * if they seek to overtake what they have aimed at."

Here "a day and a night" is an apposition to "the two 'asrs." So He swore by al-'Asr because of the lesson in it and the sign it contains. The passing of night and day, by the decree of the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing, is ordered for the interests of the world in the most perfect arrangement and system; their alternation and balance at times, one taking from the other at times, their difference in light and darkness, heat and cold, the dispersal and stillness of living creatures, and the division of the age into centuries, years, months, days, hours and what is less than these, are a sign from the signs of the Lord, the Exalted, and a proof of His power and wisdom.

So He swore by al-'Asr, which is the time of human actions and their place, concerning the outcome of those actions and their recompense. By the beginning, which is the creation of time, the agents and their actions, He drew attention to the Return, and that His power, which did not fall short of the beginning, does not fall short of the Return. And that His wisdom, which required the creation of time, the creation of agents and their actions, and making them of two kinds, good and evil, refuses to equate them, and refuses that He should reward the doer of good with the same as the doer of evil, or make both kinds winners or losers. Rather, man as such is in loss, except for those whom Allah has shown mercy, guided and enabled to have faith and righteous deeds in themselves and to enjoin them upon others. This is the counterpart of His saying ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾ and His exception of those who believe and do righteous deeds from those who are returned.

Consider the wisdom of the Qur'an: when He said ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ He restricted the exception and specified it, saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾. And when He said ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾ He widened the exception and generalized it, saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, without saying "and enjoin one another," because enjoining is the commanding of others to faith and righteous deeds, which is an additional degree beyond merely doing them. So whoever is not like this has lost this profit and is in loss, but it does not follow that he is among the lowest of the low. A person may fulfil what is obligatory upon him and not command others, since enjoining good and forbidding evil is an additional rank, which may be an individual obligation, may be a collective obligation, and may be recommended.

Enjoining one another to truth includes both truth that is obligatory and truth that is recommended, and patience includes both obligatory patience and recommended patience. Those who enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience gain the profit that those lost who merely performed what was obligatory upon them in themselves and did not command others to it. Although those were not among those who lost themselves and their families, absolute loss is one thing and utter loss is another. He, the Exalted, said ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾, and one who profits in one commodity and loses in another may be described as being in loss and having loss, as 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "We have neglected many qirats." This is a kind of negligence, and a kind of loss in relation to the one who gained that profit.

When He said in Surat al-Tin ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾, He then said ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, dividing people into only these two categories. Since man has two powers, the power of knowledge and the power of action, and two states, a state in which he is commanded by another and a state in which he commands another, He, the Exalted, excepted those whose knowledge-power is perfected by faith and whose action-power is perfected by righteous deeds, and who submit to the command of another to that effect and command others to it from among the man who is in loss. For the servant has two states: a state of perfection in himself and a state of perfecting others. His perfection and the perfecting of others depend on two things:

knowledge of the truth, and patience upon it. Thus the verse includes all the degrees of human perfection: beneficial knowledge, righteous action, benefit to oneself through these, benefit to one's brother through them, and his submission to and acceptance of one who commands him to them.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾ is a guidance to the station of leadership in the strength of religion, as in His saying ﴿And We made among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and were certain of Our signs﴾. Through patience and certainty, leadership in religion is attained.

Patience is of two kinds: patience regarding what is decreed, such as calamities, and patience regarding what is legislated.

This second kind is also of two kinds: patience in obeying commands, and patience in refraining from prohibitions.

The first is patience regarding will and action; the second is patience withholding from will and action.

As for the first kind of patience, it is shared by the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked, and no reward is given for it by itself unless it is accompanied by faith and choice.

The Prophet ﷺ said concerning his daughter:

"Order her to be patient and to seek reward."

And He, the Exalted, said ﴿except those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾.

And He, the Exalted, said ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah﴾.

And He said ﴿And if you are patient and fear Allah﴾.

So patience without faith and piety is like the strength of a body devoid of faith and piety. In proportion to certainty regarding what is legislated, patience regarding what is decreed will be.

He, the Exalted, said ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you unsteady﴾.

He commanded him to be patient and not to imitate those who have no certainty in their lack of patience, for because of their lack of certainty they lacked patience, became hasty, and made their people hasty. Had they possessed certainty and truth, they would have been patient and would not have been hasty or made others hasty. Whoever's certainty is weak, his patience is weak, and whoever's patience is weak becomes light and easily moved. The certain and patient person is steady, for he has understanding and intellect, whereas one who has no certainty and no patience is light and frivolous, played with by desires and appetites as the winds play with a light object. And Allah is the One sought for help.

(Section)

He heard a reciter recite: ﴿By time (1), indeed mankind is in loss (2), except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience (3)﴾

He said: If all the people took hold of this surah, it would suffice or encompass them, as al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If people reflected upon the surah of al-'Asr, it would suffice them."

For He, the Exalted, divided the species of man in it into two kinds: losing and profiting. The one who profits is the one who advised his own soul with faith and righteous deeds, and advised creation by enjoining the truth, which includes teaching and guiding it, and enjoining patience, which includes his own patience as well. The surah thus includes the two advices, the two perfections, and the complete perfection of the two powers, in the briefest wording, the most concise, the most refined, the finest in its eloquence, and the most delicate in its effect.

As for the two advices: the servant's advice to himself, and his advice to his brother by enjoining the truth and patience upon it.

As for the two perfections: his perfecting himself and his perfecting his brother.

As for the perfection of the two powers: the soul has two powers, the power of knowledge and reflection, whose perfection is by faith, and the power of will, love and action, whose perfection is by righteous action, and this is not completed for it except through patience.

Thus there are six matters here: three that he does in himself and commands others to: perfecting his power of knowledge by faith, and his power of action by righteous deeds, and persisting in that through patience upon it; and his command to others of these three. So he is one who is commanded to them, who commands them, who is characterized by them, who teaches them and calls to them. This is the one who profits entirely, and whatever profit he misses is in proportion to it, and some degree of loss is attained by him. And Allah is the One sought for help, and upon Him we rely.

He said in (Miftah Dar al-Sa'adah):

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿By al-'Asr, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If people reflected upon this surah entirely, it would suffice them."

The explanation of this is that the ranks are four, and by completing them a person attains the goal of his perfection:

The first: knowing the truth.

The second: acting upon it.

The third: teaching it to one who does not know it well.

The fourth: patience in learning it, acting upon it, and teaching it.

He, the Exalted, mentioned the four ranks in this surah, and He swore in this surah by al-'Asr that every person is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, who are those who knew the truth and affirmed it; this is one rank.

(and do righteous deeds): those who acted upon the truth they knew; this is another rank.

(and enjoin one another to truth): they enjoined it upon one another by teaching and guiding; this is a third rank.

(and enjoin one another to patience): they were patient upon the truth and enjoined one another to patience upon it and to steadfastness; this is a fourth rank.

This is the ultimate perfection, for perfection is that the person is perfect in himself and perfects others, and his perfection is by reforming his two powers, the knowledge-power and the action-power. The reform of the knowledge-power is by faith, and the reform of the action-power is by doing righteous deeds; his perfecting others is by teaching them and being patient with them, and by enjoining patience upon knowledge and action.

This surah, despite its brevity, is among the most comprehensive surahs of the Qur'an in encompassing all good in its entirety. Praise be to Allah, who made His Book sufficient against anything other than it, a cure for every disease, and a guide to every good.

He said in (Ighathat al-Lahfan):

He, the Exalted, swore by the age, which is the time of profitable and losing deeds, that every person is in loss, except one who perfects his knowledge-power by faith in Allah and his action-power by acting in obedience to Him. This is his perfection in himself; then he perfects others by advising them of that, commanding them to it, and to what it depends on, which is patience. Thus he perfects himself by beneficial knowledge and righteous action, and perfects others by teaching them that and advising them to be patient in it.

He said in (al-Madarij):

He, the Exalted, swore that every person is in loss, except one who perfects his knowledge-power by faith and his action-power by righteous action, and perfects others by enjoining the truth and patience upon it. The truth is faith and action, and these are not completed except by patience upon them. Enjoining one another to them makes it fitting for a person to spend the hours of his life, indeed his breaths, on what attains lofty goals through it and rescues him from manifest loss. This is achieved only by turning to the Qur'an, reflecting upon it, pondering it, extracting its treasures, unearthing its hidden things, directing attention to it, and devoting one's resolve to it, for it is the guarantor of the interests of the servants in this life and the Hereafter, and the one who leads them to the path of right guidance. Thus reality and method, and the correct states and spiritual experiences, are all obtained only from its niche and gathered only from its trees.

He said in (Uddat al-Sabirin):

He, the Exalted, judged with loss in a general judgment upon everyone who does not believe and is not among the people of truth and patience.

This indicates that no one profits other than them. He, the Exalted, said ﴿By al-'Asr, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾.

For this reason al-Shafi'i said: "If all people reflected upon this verse, it would suffice them."

That is because the servant's perfection lies in perfecting his two powers, the power of knowledge and the power of action, which are faith and righteous deeds.

Just as he needs to perfect himself, he needs to perfect others, which is enjoining one another to truth and enjoining one another to patience.

The basis of this, its foundation and its pillar on which it stands, is patience.

(Benefit)

Know that religion is built upon two principles: truth and patience, which are the two mentioned in His saying ﴿and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾.

Since what is required of the servant is to act upon the truth in himself and to implement it among people, and this is the reality of gratitude, he cannot do that except through patience upon it. Thus patience is half of faith. And Allah, the Exalted, knows best.

(Section)

Gathering with brothers is of two kinds:

One is a gathering for the comfort of the disposition and the filling of time. Its harm outweighs its benefit, and at least it corrupts the heart and wastes time.

The second is gathering with them to help one another on the means of salvation, enjoining one another to truth and patience. This is among the greatest and most beneficial gains, but it has three afflictions:

The first: some of them adorn themselves for others.

The second: speech and association beyond what is needed.

The third: that it becomes a desire and habit by which one is cut off from the goal.

In sum, gathering and association are a cross-pollination, either for the commanding soul or for the heart and the soul at peace, and the outcome is derived from the cross-pollination. Whoever seeks its right kind, his fruit will be good.

Likewise, good spirits take their cross-pollination from the angel, and wicked ones from the devil, and Allah, the Exalted, in His wisdom has made good things for good people and good people for good things.

Consider the wisdom of the Qur'an: when He said ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ He restricted the exception and specified it, saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾. And when He said ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾ He widened the exception and generalized it, saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, without saying "and enjoin one another," because enjoining is the commanding of others to faith and righteous deeds, which is an additional degree beyond merely doing them. So whoever is not like this has lost this profit and is in loss, but it does not follow that he is among the lowest of the low. A person may fulfil what is obligatory upon him and not command others, since enjoining good and forbidding evil is an additional rank, which may be an individual obligation, may be a collective obligation, and may be recommended.

Enjoining one another to truth includes both truth that is obligatory and truth that is recommended, and patience includes both obligatory patience and recommended patience. Those who enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience gain the profit that those lost who merely performed what was obligatory upon them in themselves and did not command others to it. Although those were not among those who lost themselves and their families, absolute loss is one thing and utter loss is another. He, the Exalted, said ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾, and one who profits in one commodity and loses in another may be described as being in loss and having loss, as 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "We have neglected many qirats." This is a kind of negligence, and a kind of loss in relation to the one who gained that profit.

When He said in Surat al-Tin ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾, He then said ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, dividing people into only these two categories. Since man has two powers, the power of knowledge and the power of action, and two states, a state in which he is commanded by another and a state in which he commands another, He, the Exalted, excepted those whose knowledge-power is perfected by faith and whose action-power is perfected by righteous deeds, and who submit to the command of another to that effect and command others to it from among the man who is in loss. For the servant has two states: a state of perfection in himself and a state of perfecting others. His perfection and the perfecting of others depend on two things:

knowledge of the truth, and patience upon it. Thus the verse includes all the degrees of human perfection: beneficial knowledge, righteous action, benefit to oneself through these, benefit to one's brother through them, and his submission to and acceptance of one who commands him to them.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾ is a guidance to the station of leadership in the strength of religion, as in His saying ﴿And We made among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and were certain of Our signs﴾. Through patience and certainty, leadership in religion is attained.

Patience is of two kinds: patience regarding what is decreed, such as calamities, and patience regarding what is legislated.

This second kind is also of two kinds: patience in obeying commands, and patience in refraining from prohibitions.

The first is patience regarding will and action; the second is patience withholding from will and action.

As for the first kind of patience, it is shared by the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked, and no reward is given for it by itself unless it is accompanied by faith and choice.

The Prophet ﷺ said concerning his daughter:

"Order her to be patient and to seek reward."

And He, the Exalted, said ﴿except those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾.

And He, the Exalted, said ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah﴾.

And He said ﴿And if you are patient and fear Allah﴾.

So patience without faith and piety is like the strength of a body devoid of faith and piety. In proportion to certainty regarding what is legislated, patience regarding what is decreed will be.

He, the Exalted, said ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you unsteady﴾.

He commanded him to be patient and not to imitate those who have no certainty in their lack of patience, for because of their lack of certainty they lacked patience, became hasty, and made their people hasty. Had they possessed certainty and truth, they would have been patient and would not have been hasty or made others hasty. Whoever's certainty is weak, his patience is weak, and whoever's patience is weak becomes light and easily moved. The certain and patient person is steady, for he has understanding and intellect, whereas one who has no certainty and no patience is light and frivolous, played with by desires and appetites as the winds play with a light object. And Allah is the One sought for help.

(Section)

He heard a reciter recite: ﴿By time (1), indeed mankind is in loss (2), except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience (3)﴾

He said: If all the people took hold of this surah, it would suffice or encompass them, as al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If people reflected upon the surah of al-'Asr, it would suffice them."

For He, the Exalted, divided the species of man in it into two kinds: losing and profiting. The one who profits is the one who advised his own soul with faith and righteous deeds, and advised creation by enjoining the truth, which includes teaching and guiding it, and enjoining patience, which includes his own patience as well. The surah thus includes the two advices, the two perfections, and the complete perfection of the two powers, in the briefest wording, the most concise, the most refined, the finest in its eloquence, and the most delicate in its effect.

As for the two advices: the servant's advice to himself, and his advice to his brother by enjoining the truth and patience upon it.

As for the two perfections: his perfecting himself and his perfecting his brother.

As for the perfection of the two powers: the soul has two powers, the power of knowledge and reflection, whose perfection is by faith, and the power of will, love and action, whose perfection is by righteous action, and this is not completed for it except through patience.

Thus there are six matters here: three that he does in himself and commands others to: perfecting his power of knowledge by faith, and his power of action by righteous deeds, and persisting in that through patience upon it; and his command to others of these three. So he is one who is commanded to them, who commands them, who is characterized by them, who teaches them and calls to them. This is the one who profits entirely, and whatever profit he misses is in proportion to it, and some degree of loss is attained by him. And Allah is the One sought for help, and upon Him we rely.

He said in (Miftah Dar al-Sa'adah):

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿By al-'Asr, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If people reflected upon this surah entirely, it would suffice them."

The explanation of this is that the ranks are four, and by completing them a person attains the goal of his perfection:

The first: knowing the truth.

The second: acting upon it.

The third: teaching it to one who does not know it well.

The fourth: patience in learning it, acting upon it, and teaching it.

He, the Exalted, mentioned the four ranks in this surah, and He swore in this surah by al-'Asr that every person is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, who are those who knew the truth and affirmed it; this is one rank.

(and do righteous deeds): those who acted upon the truth they knew; this is another rank.

(and enjoin one another to truth): they enjoined it upon one another by teaching and guiding; this is a third rank.

(and enjoin one another to patience): they were patient upon the truth and enjoined one another to patience upon it and to steadfastness; this is a fourth rank.

This is the ultimate perfection, for perfection is that the person is perfect in himself and perfects others, and his perfection is by reforming his two powers, the knowledge-power and the action-power. The reform of the knowledge-power is by faith, and the reform of the action-power is by doing righteous deeds; his perfecting others is by teaching them and being patient with them, and by enjoining patience upon knowledge and action.

This surah, despite its brevity, is among the most comprehensive surahs of the Qur'an in encompassing all good in its entirety. Praise be to Allah, who made His Book sufficient against anything other than it, a cure for every disease, and a guide to every good.

He said in (Ighathat al-Lahfan):

He, the Exalted, swore by the age, which is the time of profitable and losing deeds, that every person is in loss, except one who perfects his knowledge-power by faith in Allah and his action-power by acting in obedience to Him. This is his perfection in himself; then he perfects others by advising them of that, commanding them to it, and to what it depends on, which is patience. Thus he perfects himself by beneficial knowledge and righteous action, and perfects others by teaching them that and advising them to be patient in it.

He said in (al-Madarij):

He, the Exalted, swore that every person is in loss, except one who perfects his knowledge-power by faith and his action-power by righteous action, and perfects others by enjoining the truth and patience upon it. The truth is faith and action, and these are not completed except by patience upon them. Enjoining one another to them makes it fitting for a person to spend the hours of his life, indeed his breaths, on what attains lofty goals through it and rescues him from manifest loss. This is achieved only by turning to the Qur'an, reflecting upon it, pondering it, extracting its treasures, unearthing its hidden things, directing attention to it, and devoting one's resolve to it, for it is the guarantor of the interests of the servants in this life and the Hereafter, and the one who leads them to the path of right guidance. Thus reality and method, and the correct states and spiritual experiences, are all obtained only from its niche and gathered only from its trees.

He said in (Uddat al-Sabirin):

He, the Exalted, judged with loss in a general judgment upon everyone who does not believe and is not among the people of truth and patience.

This indicates that no one profits other than them. He, the Exalted, said ﴿By al-'Asr, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾.

For this reason al-Shafi'i said: "If all people reflected upon this verse, it would suffice them."

That is because the servant's perfection lies in perfecting his two powers, the power of knowledge and the power of action, which are faith and righteous deeds.

Just as he needs to perfect himself, he needs to perfect others, which is enjoining one another to truth and enjoining one another to patience.

The basis of this, its foundation and its pillar on which it stands, is patience.

(Benefit)

Know that religion is built upon two principles: truth and patience, which are the two mentioned in His saying ﴿and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience﴾.

Since what is required of the servant is to act upon the truth in himself and to implement it among people, and this is the reality of gratitude, he cannot do that except through patience upon it. Thus patience is half of faith. And Allah, the Exalted, knows best.

(Section)

Gathering with brothers is of two kinds:

One is a gathering for the comfort of the disposition and the filling of time. Its harm outweighs its benefit, and at least it corrupts the heart and wastes time.

The second is gathering with them to help one another on the means of salvation, enjoining one another to truth and patience. This is among the greatest and most beneficial gains, but it has three afflictions:

The first: some of them adorn themselves for others.

The second: speech and association beyond what is needed.

The third: that it becomes a desire and habit by which one is cut off from the goal.

In sum, gathering and association are a cross-pollination, either for the commanding soul or for the heart and the soul at peace, and the outcome is derived from the cross-pollination. Whoever seeks its right kind, his fruit will be good.

Likewise, good spirits take their cross-pollination from the angel, and wicked ones from the devil, and Allah, the Exalted, in His wisdom has made good things for good people and good people for good things.
